title: Record step machine
statement: Given a natural number $k$, a Boolean Turing machine $M$ with $k$ work tapes and state set $Q$, a function $u:T\times\mathrm{Option}(\mathrm{Bool})\to T$, a Boolean Turing machine $S$ with two work tapes and state set $S$, and designated states $s_0,s_f\in S$, the definition constructs a Turing machine with four work tapes, record symbols built from $Q$ and $T$, and control states encoding its processing stage and associated data and phase. The resulting machine is specified by the record-step transition rows, entry state, and next-state function determined by $M,u,S,s_0,s_f$; assume that $Q,T,S$ each have decidable equality.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a $k$-work-tape Boolean Turing machine with state set $Q$
$u$ maps a tag and an optional Boolean symbol to a tag
$S$ is a two-work-tape Boolean Turing machine with state set $S$
caveat: The supplied snippet does not define the record-step rows, entry state, or next-state function, so their concrete transition behavior cannot be stated.
